subject: Close-to-live MAP: Citrine Analytics rollout, migration, and training cadence
messages:

Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@citrineanalytics.com>, procurement@citrineanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-signature: MAP & pilot windows for rollout

Hi Maya —

Great to be over the finish line. I attached our first-draft Mutual Action Plan (Citrine_MAP_v1.pdf) and a spreadsheet with the evaluation prompts we plan to use. Before we lock dates, a few priorities from our side:

- Minimal-risk canary window (non-prod subset of users) for two weeks
- Migration cutover sequenced by dataset size (small -> medium -> large)
- Training: two half-day enablement sessions for platform admins and engineers
- Exec review on day 3 of canary to sign off for broader rollout

Can you confirm Redwood's recommended canary gating criteria (latency SLOs, error thresholds, rollback steps) so we can align? Also please add any dependency/ops tasks you expect us to take ownership of.

Thanks — Sofie
Sofie Park
Director, Integrations | Citrine Analytics
attachments: Citrine_MAP_v1.pdf, eval_prompts_2028.xlsx

Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature: MAP & pilot windows for rollout

Sofie —

Thanks, and congrats again. Good first pass on the MAP — I pulled it into a shared Drive and annotated a few inference-side gating points. High-level responses inline:

- Canary window: recommend 7–14 days with automated canary checks. Primary gates: 95th percentile generation latency <= 450ms, token-error (model/runtime) rate < 0.2%, and failed-streaming reconnection attempts < 0.5% per hour.
- Rollback: automated traffic split rollback to baseline model variant + 30-minute standby in Dedicated pool. We’ll maintain a warm KV cache fallback to reduce cold-start spikes.
- Migration sequencing: agree with small->medium->large. We’ll provide a migration checklist (preflight=data retention policy, network egress rules, KMS key exchange, test prompts).
- Training: can run two half-day sessions (Admin Ops + Dev integration). We suggest delivering a recorded session and a short lab exercise for your engineers.

I’m looping Marissa (on implementation delivery), Laura (on training), and Vivek (on Dedicated capacity + SLAs) to propose specific dates and a refined MAP artifact.

Next steps: Marissa will drop a proposed 6-week cadence and a canary-runbook by EOD tomorrow.

— Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 26 Apr 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature: MAP & pilot windows for rollout

Team —

Draft implementation cadence attached (see deployment_diagram.png and the MAP PDF with my inline notes). Quick summary and asks:

Week 0 (prep): exchange KMS keys, confirm VPC peering rules, validate sample dataset snapshot (low-sensitivity), and complete SOC2 evidence handoff.
Week 1 (canary week 1): route 5% traffic to Redwood Dedicated variant A, run evaluation prompts, daily canary scoreboard (latency, correctness, cost delta).
Week 2 (canary week 2): expand to 20% if gates pass; midweek exec checkpoint on day 3.
Week 3 (migration week): dataset migration in 3 waves (small/med/large) with pre-migration dry runs.
Week 4–5 (training + tuning): two enablement workshops, prompt tuning with live sessions, handback docs.
Week 6 (cutover): final switch and 72h heightened observability.

Open items for Citrine:
- Confirm admin attendees for the two workshops (names + emails)
- Provide one dataset snapshot for preflight (anonymized)
- Confirm a procurement point-of-contact for the reserved capacity contract signature and billing setup

I also added threshold values we’ll use for automated gating in the Google Drive doc. Planning to share the runbook (SUP-342) in Jira by EOD.

Marissa
Director, Customer Implementation | Redwood Inference
